title: Spec
description: One change: what, why, how it is proven, who approves it. Stored as YAML front matter in specs/<id>.md; the Markdown body holds Context, Acceptance, Design, and Non-goals.

base.description: The branch the change lands in, such as goal/booking: the goal branch of a small goal that is batched (`aidd new spec --parent` names it, or `--base`). Locally, `aidd test`, `aidd gate`, `aidd describe`, and `aidd land` compare against it and land in it when no `--base` is given. On a platform, the pull request's target decides. Default: the default branch.

title.description: One line, an imperative summary of the change, such as "Rate-limit authenticated checkout". `aidd land` writes it as the commit subject, `<type>: <title> (<ID>)`, and `aidd validate` warns when that subject passes 72 characters. `locale` may apply.

approvers.description: Eligible Approvers for this Spec. Can only narrow the config's `owners.approvers`.

route.description: normal (the gate raises it to major when the diff demands it), major, or emergency for a backfill Spec. Minor and standard changes have no Spec file.

trace_id.description: Joins the Specs and changes of one piece of work across repositories. Defaults to the id.

status.description: Optional cache of the derived status; `aidd validate` warns when it disagrees. Record only what nobody can observe: `cancelled` (a person stopped it) or `rolled_back`.

blockers.description: Role, person, or interface the Spec waits on. While it is set, the Spec is blocked: a flag `aidd list` shows, not a status.

suggested_by.description: Who suggested work nobody asked for: `agent:<role>` for an agent in `agents.proactive_roles` (or an agent account). Such a Spec stays a draft until a person records `triage`.

triage.description: A person's decision on suggested work. Required, by a person, before a Spec whose suggested_by is an agent moves past draft.

rollback.description: How to undo. Name the steps on major and emergency.

hypothesis.description: The measurable result the change should produce after Roll out, written before Spec approval and frozen by the Spec hash: a metric, its baseline, the expected move, and by when. Learn records `outcome.result` against it.

experiment.description: An A/B test that decides the `hypothesis`, planned before launch: its variants, one primary metric, the guardrails, how long it runs, and the decision rule. Optional; the product manager writes it with the tracking plan, and the flag that serves the variants is a `flags` entry. Approved content: the Spec hash covers it. `aidd validate` warns when it names no guardrail or the Spec has no hypothesis.

uat.description: True when humans accept this change by hand: a client's user acceptance test, a QA owner's manual or exploratory pass, or a device lab run. The required-docs matrix then asks for a test plan (`aidd validate` warns on major, `aidd new spec` suggests it on normal). Approved content: the Spec hash covers it.

residual_risk.description: What stays true after release. `none` when nothing remains.

adrs.description: ADR paths or links this Spec depends on, and does not change. A repository path must exist (`aidd validate`); an ADR this Spec writes is a `docs` entry of kind `adr` instead.

tasks.description: Slices of the change. Parallel only when their scope is disjoint.

files.description: Mockups, wireframes, and flows a human approves at Spec approval with the Spec, such as `specs/SPEC-220/design/**` (the Spec's own folder). Frozen by the Spec hash like the tests: never implementation scope.

design.description: The approved look and flow of a user-facing change. Optional; the product designer writes it before Spec approval.

docs.description: The documents that hold the detail this Spec links instead of carrying: a tech spec, a test plan, a prototype or design spec, an ADR, a threat model, an API contract, a migration or tracking plan, a runbook. `aidd new <kind> <topic> --spec <ID>` writes one from its template and adds the entry. A frozen doc is approved with the Spec by hash, like a design file; a living one is only checked to exist.

observe.description: Post-release check. Required on the profile's observe_required_routes: major, unless only a protected path made it major, and normal under audited.

monthly.description: What it costs to run each month at today's load, with its currency, such as `40 EUR`.

at_10x.description: The same at ten times today's load, such as `300 EUR`.

source.description: Where the numbers come from: `infracost diff`, a provider's pricing calculator, or a load test.

cost_estimate.description: What the change will cost to run, which the architect estimates in Specify: the one place for it. `aidd validate` warns on a Spec that changes infrastructure code, or whose risk names `cost`, and gives none. It also warns on a monthly estimate above `project.budget.max_infra_per_month`, the person's ceiling. Latency and availability belong in the SLO and `observe`.

flags.description: Feature flags this change ships behind, so release is separate from deploy: the architect adds one on a normal or major user-facing change that should reach users later than its code reaches production. Optional; a minor change never needs one. Approved content: the Spec hash covers it. `aidd validate` warns, and `aidd list` shows the cleanup as work, once a flag's `cleanup_due` has passed and no landed Spec lists it in `removes_flags`; a later Spec that declares the same flag with a later date extends it once that Spec lands.

removes_flags.description: Flags this change deletes from the code, by name: the cleanup Spec for an earlier Spec's `flags` entry. Once this Spec lands, `aidd validate` and `aidd list` stop reporting the flag as overdue; while it is a draft, they name it as the pending removal.

deprecations.description: What this change deprecates: an endpoint, a field, an event, a config key, or a command its consumers still use. The architect adds one when a removal or a changed meaning goes through expand and contract. The running API announces it with the `Deprecation` header (RFC 9745) and, once dated, the `Sunset` header (RFC 8594), with the same dates. Approved content: the Spec hash covers it. `aidd validate` warns, `aidd list` shows the removal as work, and `aidd digest` lists it as overdue, once its `sunset` has passed and no landed Spec lists it in `removes_deprecations`. `aidd digest --client` lists the landed ones as the deprecation calendar. A later Spec that declares the same `what` with a later `sunset` extends it once that Spec lands. Never a gate rule.

removes_deprecations.description: Deprecations this change removes from the code, by their `what`: the removal Spec for an earlier Spec's `deprecations` entry. Once this Spec lands, `aidd validate`, `aidd list`, and `aidd digest` stop reporting it; while it is a draft, they name it as the pending removal.

revisions.description: Each reopening of an approved Spec, newest last, as `aidd revise <ID> "<why>"` writes it: what was wrong and the hash that was approved. Adding one changes the Spec hash, so the approval stops holding and the Spec is a draft again: its owners change what was wrong, and the next Spec approval freezes it again. The approval card shows the latest one.

on.description: The day the Spec was reopened.

why.description: What was wrong, in one sentence.

was.description: The Spec hash that was approved before the revision.

outcome.description: What happened after Roll out. Written during the observe window and in Learn.

kind.description: What the document is. It names the role that writes it (architect: tech-spec, adr, api, migration; verifier: test-plan; product designer: design-spec (with its flows and usability test) or its HTML prototype; security engineer: threat-model, authz (the authorization matrix); SRE: runbook, slo; compliance analyst: compliance, data-map (the repository's living inventory and records of processing); product manager: analytics; delivery manager: acceptance, and vendors (the repository's vendor register)) and the required-docs matrix `aidd validate` warns from (`docs.required`).

path.description: Repo-relative path of the document, or a glob for a folder of files (a prototype with its assets), such as `specs/SPEC-220/tech-spec-limits.md`. It must match a file (`aidd validate`), and a frozen one is never a catch-all and never inside a Task's scope.

frozen.description: Default true: approved with the Spec, and part of the Spec hash like a design file, so any edit after Spec approval voids it; a drift found while implementing goes in the verification report and a later docs-only change. False for a living document several Specs revise (a runbook, an SLO, an area's architecture page): only checked to exist, and a Task that changes it names it in its scope.

scope.description: Globs this Task's diff may change: the module's folder (`src/billing/`), and a single file only where a protected path or a risk rule matches it. Never a test or design file, never a catch-all.

skeleton.description: Part of the walking skeleton: the thinnest version of a new system that runs end to end, with its structure, contracts, test runner, CI, and one smoke test, which every later slice builds on. The architect or the SRE implements it (`{skeleton}` in their write area), before the feature slices fan out. Default false.

depends_on.description: Task ids that must finish first. Required between Tasks whose scope overlaps.

skills.description: Skills loaded only for this Task, by directory name: a practice skill such as `api-design` or a stack skill, at most two. Domain packs are named in Context instead.

risk.description: What this Task could break, and how it guards against it. Approved content: frozen by the Spec hash.

proof.description: How this Task is shown to work: the test command, screenshot, or check a reviewer reads. Approved content: frozen by the Spec hash.

retry_count.description: Implementation retries used. At 3 the Task stops and the Spec is blocked until a person re-plans it.

done.description: True when the Task is finished and the evidence cannot show it (a changed scope with every command green on head shows it by itself). Bookkeeping: the Spec hash ignores it.

restored_on.description: Date service was restored after a failed change (a rollback or a fix). With `released_on`, it gives the time to restore.

learn_ref.description: Link to the retro or the PR that fed lessons back into AGENTS.md, skills, or tests.

result.description: What the metric named in `hypothesis` did after the observe window: met, missed, or inconclusive, with the number. A missed hypothesis is a Learn signal for the author and the product-manager, not a rollback.

outcome.description: What happened after Roll out. Written during the observe window and in Learn; never part of the Spec hash.

decision.description: accepted: the work goes ahead. declined: it does not, and the Spec is cancelled (a stored status must not say otherwise). snoozed: decide again on `until`; `aidd list` hides it until then. A duplicate is a relation (`duplicates`), not a triage decision.

by.description: The person who decided. Never an agent or an agent account: `aidd validate` fails one.

until.description: Snoozed only: the date the item comes back for a decision.

reason.description: Why, in one sentence. A later triage of the same idea reads it first, and links the new Spec as `duplicates`. Optional; `aidd validate` warns when a declined triage has none. Bookkeeping, like the rest of `triage`: never part of the Spec hash.

triage.description: A person's decision on work an agent suggested: accepted, declined, or snoozed, with who and when.

variants.description: The arms by name, control first, such as `["control", "one-page"]`: the variants the experiment's flag serves.

metric.description: The one primary metric that decides, the one the `hypothesis` names. Others are guardrails, or read after the decision.

guardrails.description: Metrics that must not get worse while the experiment runs (an error rate, a latency, refunds, unsubscribes); a breach stops it.

min_sample.description: Units (users, accounts, sessions) per variant before anyone reads the result, from a power calculation on the primary metric's baseline and the smallest effect worth shipping.

duration.description: How long it runs, such as `14d` or `2w`: whole weeks, so weekday effects cancel. With `min_sample`, whichever is reached last.

decision.description: The rule written before launch: when the result ships, when it stops early (a guardrail breach, a sample ratio mismatch), and what an inconclusive result means.

experiment.description: One A/B test: its variants, the primary metric, the guardrails, a minimum sample or a duration (at least one), and the decision rule.

flag_name.description: A flag key in lowercase, with `-`, `.`, or `_` between words, such as `checkout-v2`: the key the code evaluates.

default.description: The value the code falls back to when the flag system cannot answer. `off` for a new feature; `on` only for a kill switch that guards existing behavior.

owner.description: The person who decides when the flag flips and sees it removed: never an agent or an agent account (`aidd validate` fails one).

cleanup_due.description: The date by which a later Spec removes the flag and its dead branch. After it, `aidd validate` warns and `aidd list` shows the cleanup as work.

purpose.description: Why the flag exists: a release toggle, an experiment, a kill switch, or an operational toggle.

flag.description: One feature flag: its key, safe default, owner, and cleanup date.

deprecation_name.description: What is deprecated, as its consumers know it, such as `GET /v1/orders` or `order.total_cents`: the name a removal Spec lists in `removes_deprecations`.

announced.description: The day consumers were told. The `Deprecation` header (RFC 9745) carries the day the deprecation takes effect.

sunset.description: The day it stops working: the date the `Sunset` header (RFC 8594) carries, never before `announced` (`aidd validate` fails one). After it, a later Spec removes it, and until then `aidd validate` warns and `aidd list` shows the removal as work.

replacement.description: What consumers use instead, such as `GET /v2/orders`, or `none` with the reason.

consumers.description: The known consumers that still use it, as the api doc's Consumers table names them: the people told before the sunset.

deprecation.description: One deprecation: what it is, when consumers were told, when it stops working, and what replaces it.
